context: Prefer deletion. Confirm zero production callers, delete sanitize_path / anonymize_execution_metadata / anonymize_system_profile plus the config flags that only feed them, and delete or rewrite TestSanitizePath, TestAnonymizeExecutionMetadata and TestAnonymizeSystemProfile. If any caller is found, route it through _hash_public_identifier instead so the salted SHA-256 scheme is the only one in the module.
description: benchbox/core/results/anonymization.py carries a SECOND, much weaker anonymization scheme beside the public boundary hardened in PR #1512. Verified on develop at d8afb2fa9a. (1) sanitize_path('/Users/alice/bench') returns '/Users/alice/bench' UNCHANGED - the username survives because short digit-free components are kept - and the repo's own find_public_path_leaks flags that output as a leak. Same for '/home/bob/data'. (2) anonymize_system_profile emits host_{md5(hostname)[:8]} and user_{md5(username)[:8]} - UNSALTED MD5 truncated to 8 hex, trivially reversible for common hostnames and usernames - while the public boundary deliberately uses salted SHA-256 at 12 hex. (3) sanitize_path emits dir_{md5(part)[:8]} with the same weakness. Reachability: NOT currently a live leak. anonymize_execution_metadata has no caller outside itself (only self-recursion at anonymization.py:877) and nothing outside tests calls any of the three. That is why this is not critical. It is filed because it is a loaded gun in a privacy-critical module - a future caller could reasonably believe sanitize_path sanitizes - and no existing test catches the username leak (TestSanitizePath asserts only caching and long/numeric-component hashing). Not an idempotence regression either: the 8-hex tokens are not recognized by _is_public_pseudonym (12-hex), so they would be hashed once by the public boundary and then stay stable. Decide: delete the three legacy methods outright (preferred if truly unused), or make them delegate to _hash_public_identifier so one salted scheme remains.
